A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRM-Clinic study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, loss and data-selection ablations, temperature analysis, and a physician reader study of Best-of-2000 selections.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and additionally reports an outcome-only-trained ORM baseline and a ROUGE analysis of clinical notes.

M1.justification: The proposed PRM retains its clinical-step definitions, synthetic error construction, LLaMA-3.1 8B backbone, cross-entropy training and product aggregation. Expanded training and inference explanations do not establish a changed PRM procedure; the new vanilla ORM is a comparator.

E1.justification: The four main evaluation tasks and Assessment and Plan scope remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 modestly extends note-source coverage by including physician-authored notes alongside Gemini and LLaMA-Clinic notes in a comparison using cases from a prior reader study.

E2.justification: Figure 3 adds a separately trained vanilla ORM without intermediate supervision, providing an important outcome-only control absent from v1. The earlier same-checkpoint ORM remains as 'ORM (Ours)', alongside the retained Gemini Pro 1.0 and 1.5 comparators.

E3.justification: v1 Appendix B.3 evaluates ORM verification by checking whether the gold note's final predicted label is '+'. v2 Appendix B.4 instead checks whether ORM ranks the gold note first among candidates, matching the PRM selection criterion. This substantially revises the reported comparison protocol. Appendix C.3 also introduces ROUGE-1, ROUGE-L and ROUGE-Lsum comparisons.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.3 analyzes similarity between physician, Gemini and LLaMA-Clinic notes to investigate strong out-of-distribution performance. Existing loss/data-selection ablation designs, temperature analysis, physician-study comparisons and example-based analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point accuracies and descriptive physician win/tie/loss percentages. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests; v2 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: ORM verification results change extensively under the revised criterion. For the best PRM checkpoint, Table 3's ORM scores change from 61.3% to 98.8% on A-Verify, 83.8% to 97.5% on Dialogue-G, and 90.0% to 100.0% on A-Validate. These are revised-protocol results, not demonstrated same-setting model gains. v2 also adds vanilla ORM and ROUGE results; PRM scores and physician-study outcomes remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The cross-entropy objective and four token-selection loss definitions remain mathematically equivalent. The general objective moves from Appendix A into Section 3.3; no substantive derivation, assumption, theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central comparative claim is redefined. v1 claims superiority over its same-checkpoint ORM across tasks; v2's abstract and introduction emphasize superiority over the newly trained vanilla ORM. Section 4.1 explicitly reports comparable verification performance against its own ORM, retaining the preference-selection advantage. The broader contribution of scalable clinical process supervision remains.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes the benefit of step-level training from aggregating step scores and interprets cross-source ROUGE similarity as context for strong generalization. New discussion addresses deployment monitoring, validation on real-world data and possible open-source synthesis alternatives. Limitations additionally acknowledge the small evaluation dataset and proprietary Gemini dependency.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 specifies how to construct the vanilla ORM: replace intermediate score labels with placeholders, retain the final label, and otherwise preserve the corpus and training pipeline. Existing PRM hyperparameters, hardware information, prompts and code-access disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds several references and Appendix E, discussing DeepSeek-R1's objections to PRMs and positioning process supervision alongside rule-based reinforcement learning and recent test-time scaling work. The established clinical-note and process-supervision positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten, and the approach is reorganized into problem formulation, construction, training, usage and evaluation. The former standalone Experimental Settings section is integrated into Section 3, the A&P rationale moves to Appendix D.3, and new discussion and related-work appendices reshape the narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn with an additional comparator, revised legend, colors and axis ranges. Figure 2 and Table 1 move; table captions and emphasis are refined. Appendix Table 2 redisplays the existing ORM result as 'Last', and a new ROUGE table is added. Other figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: v1 used different verification criteria for PRM and ORM and lacked a separately trained outcome-only control. v2 reports a matched Best-of-N criterion, adds that control, and revises the interpretation accordingly (Appendix B, Figure 3 and Table 3). This resolves an important deficiency in the central comparison and substantially improves its validity and interpretability. The small physician evaluation and absent uncertainty estimates remain limitations.
